Nvidia's stock jumped about thirty percent in one morning. Why? Its CEO is back.
On November twelfth, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO. The company's filing gave no reason. The CFO, Colette Kress, stepped in as interim CEO.
Then the stock fell seven trading days in a row.
This morning, the board voted unanimously to bring him back, effective immediately. At the opening bell, Nvidia jumped almost thirty-two percent, to about one sixty-five a share.
An independent committee is still looking into reports that a foreign intelligence effort targeted him.
Out for eleven days, then back on top. Right call? Tell me in the comments.
